summary: “Most Protective” tier in the July 2026 assessment: regional non-discrimination covering gender identity and shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state actions; no state-specific negative finding beyond the shared federal layer (passport/API policy, priced into the national score).. Washington is singled out in the map's protective-tier text as one of the states that have enacted comprehensive health-insurance laws covering facial-hair removal and an expanded range of medical procedures.

sources.summary: July 2026 anti-trans legal-risk assessment map (Erin In The Morning, republication): scores every US state for transgender adults and lists Washington among the fifteen 'Most Protective' states (CA, CO, CT, HI, IL, MA, MD, MN, NJ, NM, NY, OR, RI, VT, WA), naming it specifically with Colorado, Hawaii and Maryland as states with comprehensive health-insurance laws covering facial-hair removal and an expanded range of medical procedures, with refugee protections for people fleeing restrictive states. The same update moved Idaho to 'Do Not Travel' and rated the country overall 'Worst Policies In Effect'.

Movement Advancement Project equality map (data as of 25 Sep 2026): 16 states plus DC have 'shield' laws protecting access to transgender health care - shielding recipients and providers from civil or criminal actions by states where care is banned; 38% of the transgender population (13+) lives under a shield law, 56% under none. Washington is among the shield-law states cited in the dossier's 'Most Protective' line for this unit.

localsOnly: The comprehensive insurance-coverage mandate the July 2026 map names Washington for is a resident-facing detail; it shapes care access, not a visitor's exposure.
